references.text: Prohibition against sacrificing children to Molech, the specific idol associated with child sacrifice that Deuteronomy 12:31 warns against.
The punishment for sacrificing children to Molech, which elaborates on the seriousness of the abomination mentioned in Deuteronomy 12:31.
King Ahaz had his son pass through the fire, an example of the pagan practice condemned in Deuteronomy 12:31.
The Israelites had their sons and daughters pass through the fire, fulfilling the warning against imitating pagan sacrificial practices.
King Manasseh had his son pass through the fire, a direct violation of the prohibition in Deuteronomy 12:31.
King Josiah destroyed Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom to prevent child sacrifice to Molech.
The prophet Jeremiah condemns child sacrifice as an abominable practice that God never commanded.
The Lord says that child sacrifice in Topheth never came into His heart, a strong rejection of this pagan practice.
Condemnation of burning sons as offerings to Baal, something the Lord never commanded.
Ezekiel condemns Jerusalem's practice of sacrificing their children to idols.
The Lord confronts Israel with their child sacrifice and idolatry.
The psalmist describes how Israel sacrificed their sons and daughters to the idols in Canaan.
